meta.title: Verified tax rules relevant to a sale-versus-renewal comparison
meta.scope: Only rules that were read verbatim on an official IRS or California Franchise Tax Board page during this session. Every rule below is a rule, not a computation about the owner. No owner figures (basis, gain, income, state of residence) are present or guessed.
meta.warning: These rules are inputs to a calculator, not advice. Two of them (depreciation method and state of residence) are determinative and are currently unknown.

federal.detail: For taxable years beginning in 2025 the tax rate on most net capital gain is no higher than 15% for most individuals. 0% applies if taxable income is at or below $48,350 single / $96,700 married filing jointly / $64,750 head of household. 15% applies above those up to $533,400 single / $600,050 MFJ / $566,700 HoH. 20% applies to the extent taxable income exceeds the 15% thresholds.
federal.source_name: IRS Topic no. 409, Capital gains and losses

federal.rule: Unrecaptured section 1250 gain is taxed at a maximum 25%
federal.detail: IRS Topic 409 lists 'the portion of any unrecaptured section 1250 gain from selling section 1250 real property is taxed at a maximum 25% rate.' This is the depreciation that was taken (or allowable) on the building and is recaptured on sale at up to 25% rather than at the 20% capital-gain maximum.
federal.source_name: IRS Topic no. 409, Capital gains and losses

federal.rule: Net Investment Income Tax at 3.8% above modified AGI thresholds
federal.detail: The NIIT applies at 3.8% to certain net investment income of individuals with income above statutory thresholds: $250,000 MFJ, $125,000 MFS, $200,000 single, $200,000 head of household, $250,000 qualifying widow(er). The thresholds are not indexed for inflation. Gains from the sale of investment real estate (including a second home that is not a primary residence) are included in net investment income.
federal.source_name: IRS, Questions and Answers on the Net Investment Income Tax

federal.rule: Section 1031 like-kind exchange defers gain; real property only
federal.detail: Under the Tax Cuts and Jobs Act, section 1031 applies only to exchanges of real property. Real properties are generally like-kind regardless of whether improved or unimproved. Real property in the United States is not like-kind to real property outside the United States. Reported on Form 8824.
federal.source_name: IRS, Like-kind exchanges — Real estate tax tips
federal.used_by: after-tax module (deferral branch); the 1031 path requires an identified replacement and a qualified intermediary, neither of which exists yet

federal.rule: Land is never depreciable; buildings are
federal.detail: IRS: 'Land is never depreciable, although buildings and certain land improvements may be.' Property placed in service after 1986 generally must use MACRS. A restaurant building is nonresidential real property; the allocation between the nondepreciable land and the depreciable building determines the recapture exposure on sale.

federal.rule: MACRS recovery period for nonresidential real property
federal.detail: Not read during this session. IRS Publication 946 is the controlling source; the specific 39-year versus 31.5-year distinction by placed-in-service date was not transcribed here.
federal.source_name: IRS Publication 946, How To Depreciate Property
federal.used_by: flagged as unverified; the calculator therefore asks for accumulated depreciation directly instead of deriving it

california.rule: California has no lower rate for capital gains
california.detail: Franchise Tax Board: 'California does not have a lower rate for capital gains. All capital gains are taxed as ordinary income.' Reported on California Schedule D (540).
california.source_name: California Franchise Tax Board, Capital gains and losses (last updated 2026-01-28)
california.used_by: after-tax module (state rate applied to the full gain)

california.rule: California 2025 rate schedules (used for the top marginal rate)
california.source_name: California Franchise Tax Board, 2025 California Tax Rate Schedules
California Franchise Tax Board, 2024 California Tax Rate Schedules
california.used_by: comparison of bracket drift; 2026 schedules were not published at the time of reading

california.rule: California requires FTB 3840 when California property is exchanged for out-of-state property
california.detail: For taxable years beginning on or after 1 January 2014, R&TC sections 18032 and 24953 require California resident and nonresident taxpayers who defer gain on the sale or exchange of California property for out-of-state replacement property under IRC 1031 to file an annual information return. All taxpayers, regardless of residence, who exchange California real property for like-kind property outside California must file form FTB 3840.
california.source_name: FTB Publication 1100, 2025 Taxation of Nonresidents and Individuals Who Change Residency
california.used_by: after-tax module (California-source gain retention on a 1031 out of state)

california.rule: California sources real-property gain to where the property is located
california.detail: FTB: 'California taxes real property based upon where the property is located.' Example 16 in Publication 1100: a Texas resident exchanges a California condominium for Texas property, defers a $15,000 gain, later sells the Texas property recognising $20,000; the $15,000 deferred gain 'has a source in California and is taxable by California.'
california.used_by: important if OWNER-1 is not a California resident: moving out of state does not remove California tax on this property's gain

california.rule: Proposition 13 assessment and the 2% annual cap; reassessment on change of ownership
california.detail: Los Angeles County Assessor: Proposition 13 'limits a property owner's general levy tax to 1 percent of the assessed value' and 'mandated that a property's assessed value could not increase by more than 2 percent from one year to the next except in the event of a change in ownership, new construction, the property receives a temporary decline in assessed value (Proposition 8), or the property is designated a restricted historical property (Mills Act).'
california.used_by: hold-case carrying cost; a sale resets the buyer's basis and therefore the buyer's tax, which affects the price a buyer can pay

california.detail: The Assessor states that it will begin accepting Decline-in-Value applications for the 2026-2027 tax year on 2 July 2026 and that the deadline to file is 30 November 2026.
california.used_by: a downside hedge on the hold case; not modelled in the calculator because no assessed value is known

labour_cost.detail: Division of Labor Standards Enforcement: 'Effective January 1, 2026, the minimum wage is $16.90 per hour for all employers, not otherwise covered by a higher minimum wage specific to an industry or a locality.' After reaching $15 the rate is adjusted annually by CPI-W, cannot be lowered, and is capped at a 3.5% annual increase.
labour_cost.source_name: California Department of Industrial Relations, Minimum Wage FAQ
labour_cost.used_by: tenant cost pressure; the single largest operating input at a quick-service restaurant

labour_cost.detail: The Industrial Relations FAQ confirms a higher minimum wage for fast-food workers effective 1 April 2024 and links to a dedicated FAQ. The specific current dollar rate was not read from an official page during this session.
labour_cost.source_name: California Department of Industrial Relations, Minimum Wage FAQ (fast-food link)
labour_cost.used_by: flagged: the widely reported $20.00 rate was NOT confirmed on an official page here, so it is not used as a value

local_tax_note.rule: City of Los Angeles business tax and any local transfer tax
local_tax_note.detail: Not read during this session. Los Angeles imposes a real property transfer tax by documentary stamp, and a city business tax on gross receipts; neither rate was confirmed on an official page here.
local_tax_note.source_name: City of Los Angeles Office of Finance (not read)
local_tax_note.used_by: left out of the calculator entirely rather than guessed
